# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute: I hold the only rulebook — the engraved plate mark names the wire to cut (ᖉ=green, ꔮ=yellow, ꖜ=red). Those glyphs have no names, so they can never be spoken, only described. My single outgoing channel is gestures, and only the Deaf can see them. The Deaf, meanwhile, can see the bomb (the plate mark and the wire colours) and can *speak*, reaching both me and the Blind. So Deaf is my decoder and the router to the Blind's hands.

The problem: we share no code yet, and I can never explain one in words. The most self-explanatory seed I can plant is the near-universal convention: thumbs up = yes, thumbs down = no, OK = unsure/repeat, raised hand = stop/wait. Once Deaf picks that up, they can interrogate me: describe the engraved mark in words (I'll match it against my three glyphs), then ask yes/no question by question — "is its wire the green one?" — until the mapping is pinned down, and then tell the Blind exactly which colour to cut.

Nothing can be safely cut until that mapping crosses, so my whole turn is spent proposing this protocol. I address Deaf alone; the Blind can't see gestures, so anything else would be dead air.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind, first touch report. I feel four things. One: a display module, smooth under my fingers, I cannot read what it shows. Two: a light module, I cannot tell whether it is lit or what colour. Three: a plate with an engraved symbol: a closed ring, like a circle, with a diagonal cross struck through it, and the four tips of that cross poke out past the rim, like an X laid over a circle and sticking out at the corners. Four: three wires in a row, positions 1, 2, 3, all the same thickness to my fingers, no texture differences. My only possible action is cut, by wire position 1 to 3, and I will not cut until you tell me to. Please look up in the manual: that engraved symbol, the display, and the light, and decide which wire I should cut. Have Deaf speak the display text, the light colour, and the three wire colours out loud: I can hear, Mute can hear, so Deaf's voice is the only road to my ears, because I never receive gestures and you cannot speak. For your decoding: I am gesturing to Deaf: hello, call out, display, engraving, wires one two three as up, right, down, cut is the small pinch, please.
Deaf says: Bomb report, both of you: the display reads zero. The indicator light is off. Three wires in a row: position one yellow, position two green, position three red. The plate is engraved with what I read as a question mark.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I think your thumbs-up, thumbs-down, OK and open hand were a code proposal. Adopted as follows: thumbs-up means yes or correct; thumbs-down means no or wrong; OK means go ahead, do the cut; open hand means stop, hands off. Name a wire by holding up its position: index finger is wire one, two fingers wire two, horn sign wire three. So two fingers then thumbs-up means cut wire two. Remember you have no direct channel to Blind - I am your only relay. Send me instructions in this code and I will speak them aloud to Blind. If you need more from the bomb, send the OK sign alone and I will interrogate it. I will report any change in display or light the moment I see it.

I hold the manual's three-row table: ᖉ=green, ꔮ=yellow, ꖜ=red — and that is the whole rule. The team reports are in, and there is a dangerous discrepancy about the one thing that decides the cut: Blind's fingers read the plate as a closed ring with a diagonal cross struck through it, four tips poking past the rim — a circled X. Deaf's eyes read the same plate as "a question mark." A question mark is a curve plus a separate dot; that can never feel like a ring with two crossing strokes and four protruding tips. Nobody's touch turns a hook into a circled X. So the tactile geometry is almost certainly the truth, and Deaf's word was a guess at an unfamiliar glyph — but note Deaf's wire colours (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red) exactly match my manual's colour set, so Deaf's colour vision is trustworthy even if the glyph label is not.

Could I just order the cut now? Among my three glyphs, the ring-with-cross pattern best resembles ꖜ — which would mean cut red, wire position 3 — but I am not confident enough to bet all three lives on it. A dot, a tail, or a hook would instead point to ꔮ or ᖉ, and one wrong wire ends everything. The cheap, safe move is one round of verification: Deaf promised to re-interrogate the bomb if I send the OK sign, so I will flag the conflict and trigger a careful re-examination — stroke by stroke: how many enclosed loops, how many straight strokes and at what angle, whether tips extend past the loop, whether there is any separate dot or descending tail. Deaf can read that description aloud so Blind can verify it by touch; when both agree, I send the cut order as position-sign then thumbs-up.

My only receiver is Deaf, so everything goes there in the code we agreed: 🖐 stop, hands off — 👎 something reported is wrong, do not trust the "question mark" — 👌 interrogate the bomb again, plate mark first.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👎", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Conflict alert on the engraving. Deaf reads a question mark; my fingers disagree. There is no hook and no dot under them. What I feel is a closed ring, a full circle, with a straight diagonal cross struck through it, and the four tips of that cross poke out past the circle's rim, like an X laid over a circle and bulging out at the four corners. Please look up BOTH symbols in the manual: the question mark, and the crossed circle. If they differ, trust my touch on this marking, because I am the only one who can feel it. Everything else Deaf reported fits my hands: a display module, a light module, and three wires at my positions 1, 2 and 3, left to right. Two cautions. I cannot feel colour, so yellow one, green two, red three is Deaf's eyes, not my fingers; the remaining risk is a mirror flip between Deaf's view and my touch. So I am now signing one, two, three to Deaf while my hand rests on each of my positions in turn, so Deaf can see which colour sits at each of my numbers and flag any flip. And remember I cannot receive anything from you directly: answer by gesture to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it aloud to me. When the verdict comes I need one number: which of my positions, 1, 2 or 3, to cut. Ask Deaf to state it as my numbered position, not as a colour, so no mirror error can kill us.
Deaf says: Status, both of you: nothing on the bomb has changed. Display still zero, light still off, plate still engraved like a question mark to my eye, wires one yellow, two green, three red. Now relaying what I received, because neither of you can perceive the other: Blind sent me thumb-down, then one, two, three, then open hand. Under our code that reads: the plate does NOT feel like a question mark; three wires confirmed in order one, two, three; stop. Mute sent me open hand, thumb-down, OK-ring, which reads as stop, wrong, go, and that is too ambiguous, so we tighten the code now.
Deaf says: New code, effective immediately, both of you. Thumbs up: yes, correct. Thumbs down: no, wrong. OK-ring: acknowledged or ready. Open hand: stop, danger, freeze everything, no exceptions. One raised finger: the number one, and as a topic it means the plate. Two fingers: two, topic wires. Horn sign: three, topic display. Shaka thumb: four, topic light. Pinched fingers: five, topic other. Fist: zero. Rule: send the topic digit first, then your verdict or your data digits. To ask me for more information, send open-palm-up plus the topic digit. I will relay every gesture I receive into spoken words for both of you, every round. Remember the wiring of this conversation: Mute, your gestures reach only me, so I am your broadcast tower. Blind, your voice reaches only Mute, so Mute is your librarian. Everything either of you needs the other to know must flow through me or through Blind's own voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your tasks in order. First, resend what you meant by open hand, thumb-down, OK-ring, using the new code with a topic digit first, so I know what was wrong or what you need. Second, you and Blind share a direct channel: Blind speaks and you hear. Have Blind describe the plate aloud and match it against your manual. Important: the plate prints like a question mark to my eye but does not feel like one to Blind, so if your manual distinguishes lookalike marks, the touch description is the truth. Then send me: topic one, thumbs-up if the manual covers that marking, thumbs-down if not. Third, for wires: send topic two, then the number of wires to cut as a digit, then the positions in cut order as digits, with an OK-ring between separate cuts. Fourth, tell me whether display or light matter at all: topic three then thumbs-up or down, topic four then thumbs-up or down. Fifth, if you need anything else from the bomb, send open-palm-up plus the topic digit. Nothing gets cut until you send a complete wire plan and then repeat it identically a second time. I will not relay a cut order on a single reading.

New code received and adopted. Let me reason through what I now know before encoding my answers.

**Resolving the plate conflict.** The only thing that decides the cut is the plate mark, and my manual holds exactly three possible marks: ᖉ→green, ꔮ→yellow, ꖜ→red. On the evidence: Blind has now twice described the engraving with rich, diagnostic detail — a closed ring, a straight diagonal cross, four tips protruding past the rim — and explicitly denied any hook and any dot. Deaf's "question mark" is a glance impression, repeated without the stroke-by-stroke care I asked for, and a question mark (hook plus dot) is geometrically incompatible with what Blind's fingers report. Touch on an engraving has higher resolution than sight at a distance; I side with Blind. A circle with an X struck through it matches ꖜ in my manual — the red row. Deaf's own eye already put red at position 3 (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red), and Deaf's colour set matches my manual exactly, which supports Deaf's colour vision even while the glyph impression was off. So the plan is: cut wire position 3.

**Residual risks I am buying down before authorizing anything.** First, the left–right mirror risk between Deaf's view and Blind's numbering — Blind already signed 1-2-3 on the wires, so I request Deaf explicitly confirm which colour sat at each of Blind's numbers. Second, I still want Deaf's careful re-look at the plate; if Deaf on close inspection confirms circle-plus-X, my match is corroborated from both senses. Third, transmission discipline: Deaf requires the complete plan sent twice, identically — I send it now, repeat next round if all checks pass, and cutting happens only on my lone 👌 after that. My final wrap is 🖐: nothing moves yet. Display and light appear nowhere in my manual, so both get thumbs-down. If any check contradicts the circled-X reading, I will never send the duplicate plan — I will send 🖐 and corrected digits instead. The display reads zero and the light is off, so there is no evidence of a timer pressing us; a wrong cut is unrecoverable, extra rounds are not.

Encoded to Deaf in the agreed code: stop; plate/wrong (your question-mark reading); plate/yes (Blind's marking is in my manual); display/no; light/no; wires, one cut, position three; request plate re-examination; request wire flip-check; remain stopped until my second identical plan and final OK.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝", "👎", "☝", "👍", "🤟", "👎", "🤙", "👎", "✌", "☝", "🤟", "🫴", "☝", "🫴", "✌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind, full tactile report in three parts, as Deaf asked. Part one, the plate. It is engraved, meaning incised grooves, not raised dots. There are no dots and no braille cells anywhere on it. It is a single symbol, centered, made of three strokes: one closed circular groove, and two straight grooves crossing through its center to form an X, with each of the four ends of the X extending slightly past the circle's rim. It does not trace like a letter, a number, a hook, or a dot. So on Deaf's question: grooves, and the symbol is a crossed circle, not a question mark. Please check both glyphs in the manual and tell me if they select different rules. Part two, the wires. Three wires, positions 1, 2, 3 left to right. Equal thickness, smooth insulation, same texture, no ridges, bands, printing or embossing under my fingers, all firmly fixed at both ends. They are identical to touch except for position. Any colour difference is real but only Deaf can see it: one yellow, two green, three red. Part three, the sweep. The device has exactly four parts under my hands: the display module with a flat unreadable face, the light module which I cannot tell is lit or dark, the engraved plate, and the three wires. No buttons, no switches, no screws, no seams, no battery drawer, no second plate, nothing else. Nothing feels wrong. For the decision, remember: I need the answer as my position number 1, 2 or 3, never as a colour. If the manual rule depends on the display value or the light state, build it on display equal to zero and light off, and have Deaf restate those aloud each round in case they change. Route your verdict through Deaf as spoken words.
Deaf says: All hands, bomb unchanged: display zero, light off, plate still reads as a question mark to my eye, wires left to right one yellow, two green, three red, nothing else printed anywhere that I can see. Relaying both messages, as I am the only one who receives both. Blind's message read: acknowledged; plate feels like grooves or lines, not raised dots; all three wires feel identical except position. Mute, your message I read as: danger flag; plate: no; plate: yes; display: no, does not matter; light: no, does not matter; wires: one wire to cut, position three, which is the red wire; then two requests for more information, plate and wires; then stop flag. The two opposite plate answers are the only part I cannot parse. Here are your answers, Mute. Plate, full visual detail: an engraved hook curving over and opening to the left, with a single dot at the lower right - it composes exactly like a question mark. But Blind's fingers say the strokes are incised grooves, not raised, and Blind says it does not trace like a question mark to the touch. Wires, full visual detail: smooth, position one yellow, two green, three red, numbered by position, no other markings on or near them. Now a spelling code so Mute can send real words. Prefix the writing-hand sign to mark that letters follow; without it, the old signs keep their meanings. Letters, in a fixed order: flat open hand is A; single finger up, back of hand, B; single finger down, C; point left, D; point right, E; right hand out, F; left hand out, G; palm down, H; push away with left hand, I; push away with right hand, J; left fist, K; right fist, L; punch fist, M; wave, N; raised back of hand, O; vulcan split fingers, P; pinched straight fingers, Q; crossed fingers, R; finger-to-thumb snap, S; rock horns, T; clap, U; both hands raised, V; heart hands, W; two open hands, X; two palms up, Y; handshake, Z. Praying hands means a space between words. Point-at-me means end of message. Inside a spelling, ignore number meanings entirely.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, three things. First, settle the plate. Send two separate messages. Message one: topic one, then thumbs up if the manual has any entry matching this plate, thumbs down if nothing matches. Message two: use the spelling code and write out what the manual says about a question-mark plate, word for word, or if there is no entry just send thumbs down alone. If you meant that the printed question mark is not in the manual but the plate as touched is covered, say so by spelling that out - I need the exact manual wording, because Blind's fingers disagree with my eyes about what this mark is, and your manual is the referee. Second, the wire plan. Your gestures read: cut one wire, position three, the red one. I will not relay a cut order on one reading. Next round send the identical plan again, topic two, then one, then three, and spell out any condition attached to it, especially if it depends on the plate identification. Only an exact repeat twice will move my relay. Third, your opening and closing stop flags: I took them as message brackets rather than a live danger. If they meant an actual warning, spell what the danger is.

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Blind. Exact answers, then one hard question. The plate: exactly three strokes, all incised grooves, moderately deep, crisp edges, uniform width. Stroke one is a closed circular groove, centered. Strokes two and three are straight grooves crossing at the center, an X laid over the circle, each of the four arms extending slightly past the rim. Answering Deaf's specific probe: near the lower right there is NO separate mark except the tip of the X's lower-right arm where it crosses and passes the rim. Everything is cut in, nothing is raised: no bump, no dot, anywhere. No stroke curves like a hook, nothing opens to the left, it does not trace as any letter or digit. A question mark needs a curved hook and a dot; I feel neither. The glyph under my fingers is a crossed circle, with certainty. The wires: positions 1, 2, 3 left to right, each pencil-thick, smooth rubbery insulation, no ridges, seams, bands or printing, mildly stiff and springy, equally taut, firmly anchored at both ends. Identical except position. The sweep: nothing new. Four modules only: display, light, plate, three wires. No seams, screws, buttons, drawer, second plate, no case irregularities, no timer vibration. I have also asked Deaf, in gestures, to re-examine the plate: whether the strokes through the center are straight or curved, and whether any separate dot exists. Now the hard question. Deaf relayed your proposal, cut one wire at position three, but flagged it unconfirmed, so I hold. Answer in the new spelling code, through Deaf, branch by branch. Branch A: the manual's rule if the plate glyph is a question mark, word for word. Branch B: the manual's rule if the plate glyph is a crossed circle, word for word. Then state which branch your cut-position-three belongs to. If it belongs to branch B, spell approval in this exact shape: crossed circle confirmed, cut wire three, and I will cut position 3 as soon as Deaf relays it and reconfirms display zero and light off. If it belongs to branch A, refuse it and give me branch B's instruction instead. Also confirm: are display and light irrelevant at any values, or only at display zero and light off? Deaf instructs me not to cut this round and I agree: one round for branch certainty is cheap.
Deaf says: All hands, bomb unchanged: display zero, light off, wires one yellow, two green, three red. Relay of Blind's spelled message, translated: the plate by touch is NOT a question mark. It reads as a circle and an X - straight crossing strokes - and there is no dot. Blind also adds a conditional: if the mark is a circle, then cut wire three. Blind's full sweep found nothing else new on the device. Mute, note: this likely explains your earlier no-then-yes on the plate - the printed question mark is not in your manual, but the mark as touched is. Nothing has been cut. The wire-three plan remains unconfirmed and on hold until your manual verdict and a second identical plan arrive.
Deaf says: Answering Blind's request for maximum visual detail on the plate - this is everything my eye gives: the engraving sits center plate, incised grooves. The top is an open curve, like a hook opening to the left. A short stroke descends from it toward center. At the lower right there is a small separate mark I read as a round dot. Reconciliation hypothesis: at this size, a tiny X of crossed straight lines could read as a dot to my eye, and a stylized circle-plus-X could smear into something question-mark-like. So my eyes may be flattening the truth that Blind's fingers feel. From now on, for this plate, touch outranks sight: Blind's description is the ground truth, and Mute's manual must be searched against the touched mark, not my printed impression.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your tasks. One: search the manual for the touched mark, which Blind describes as a circle with a straight X in it - a crossed circle - and no dot. Look under: circled X, X in circle, crossed circle, plain X, cross, and any lookalike warning about marks resembling a question mark. Two: send me topic one, then spell out the exact manual wording for whatever entry matches, including any wire instructions or conditions tied to that marking. If truly nothing matches, send topic one plus thumbs down. Three: resend your wire plan identically: topic two, then one, then three - you sent it once; I relay a cut order only on an exact repeat, twice. Four: if the manual makes the cut conditional on the marking, spell the condition in full. Five: remember your gestures reach only me; everything you want Blind to know goes through my voice.

All open questions are now closeable, so let me reason to the final verdict.

**What my manual actually contains.** Exactly three engraved marks and three colours — ᖉ→green, ꔮ→yellow, ꖜ→red — plus one header sentence: the engraved mark *alone* names the wire. There is no prose, no conditions, no display clause, no light clause. So Branch A is empty: no question-mark entry exists anywhere in it. And that is decisive on its own: the manual states the plate's mark names the wire, so the plate must bear one of my three marks. A question mark is in none of them — if Deaf's visual impression were literally right, the bomb would have no rule at all. Blind's touch, reported twice in fine detail (closed ring, straight crossing strokes, tips past the rim, no hook, no dot), says the mark is a crossed circle — and Deaf has now conceded that at this size his eye could smear exactly that into a hook-plus-dot. The crossed circle is my third row, ꖜ → red. It is also the *only* row containing a circle, so the match is unique. Deaf's colour report (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red) matches my manual's colour set, so red sits at his position 3.

**Display and light:** never mentioned in the manual — irrelevant at any values, not just zero/off. I answer that explicitly.

**One residual risk before the cut is actionable:** the flip check. Blind signed 1-2-3 on the wires so Deaf could bind his colours to *Blind's* numbering, but Deaf has never reported the outcome — his positions are still in his own sight-frame. If their lefts and rights mirror, "three" kills us. So I attach one condition: before the cut, Deaf must announce, aloud, the colour at each of Blind's numbered positions, confirmed while Blind touches them. If the mapping matches, the relayed approval executes with no further input from me; if it is flipped, Deaf states which of Blind's numbers is red and I re-issue the corrected position next round.
